Disband's status page is self-hosted. It does not depend on a third-party status service, so it can still report accurately when the main web host, API, or stat

The page groups monitors by service. For each monitor it shows: - the current state from the latest check; - the HTTP status and response time of that check; - a 90-day uptime bar, one segment per day; - the last time a check ran. Below the monitors are incidents, scheduled maintenance, and announcements. Each opens a detail page with the full update timelin

Automated checks run every minute and record one result per monitor. A monitor is healthy only when its expected HTTP status matches and any configured keyword is present. Timeouts, network errors, wrong statuses, and missing keywords are recorded as failures. Checks run independently of the web app, so a failure at the web host does not stop checks being re

Each check is stored and rolled up into daily history, so the 90-day uptime bar is read from precomputed data rather than aggregated on demand. - Raw checks are retained for 90 days. - Daily roll-ups are retained for 180 days. - The public page displays the latest 90 days. - Each day's segment is the percentage of successful checks that day. When a monitor fails three checks in a row, a major incident is opened automatically and linked to that monitor. When the next check succeeds, the incident is resolved with an update describing the outage duration. The incident remains visible with its full history.
